name: RÄƒzboi
description: RÄƒzboi (Romanian for 'War') is a classic, high-energy card game of chance played primarily by children and families in Romania. While globally known as 'War', the Romanian variant features specific point-values for face cards (often treated as 10s) and a unique 'Escalation' rule for ties, where the number of cards laid down during a conflict depends on the rank of the card that triggered the war. It is a game of pure persistence and endurance.

history.origins: Part of the ancient 'Battle' family of card games that appeared in Europe in the 17th century. The Romanian version, RÄƒzboi, has been a cultural staple in schools and villages for generations.
timeline: 1800s: Traditional 'War' variants become popular in the Balkans.
1950s: RÄƒzboi is standardized in Romanian youth publications.
Present: One of the most common introductory card games in modern Romania.
history.cultural: In Romania, 'RÄƒzboi' is often the first card game a child learns from their grandparents.
history.evolution: The game evolved into a simple educational tool for teaching children number comparison and the value of perseverance.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card French deck; Ace ranks high. The deck is divided evenly among the players. Suits are ignored; only rank matters for battles and wars.
setup.dealing: Deal the entire deck equally (26 cards each for 2 players). Cards are kept in a face-down stack; players never look at their own cards.

rules.objective: Win all 52 cards by winning battles and wars. Higher card wins each battle (Ace high). On tie, escalation war: number of face-down cards depends on the rank that caused the tie (e.g. 7 to 7 cards, King to 10, Ace to 11); then one face-up card decides; repeat until one player wins the pile.
rules.gameplay: 1. Both players flip top card. 2. Higher wins; winner takes both to bottom. 3. Tie = War: lay cards face-down by rank (7â†’7 cards, Kâ†’10, Aâ†’11); flip last; higher wins all. 4. Repeat War if last cards tie. 5. Win all 52 cards.
keyRules: Simultaneous flip of top card from each player's stack.
Higher rank wins the battle (Ace high); winner takes both cards to bottom of stack.
Tie triggers war: escalation by rank (e.g. 7 lays 7 face-down, King 10, Ace 11), then one face-up; higher wins all.
Repeat war if face-up cards tie; game ends when one player has all 52 cards.

strategy.basic: Pure Chance. RÄƒzboi is a game of zero-volition; the deck order is fixed once dealt. However, in physical play, the way you place won cards at the bottom of your deck matters. Grouping face-cards together can lead to 'Streaks' that allow you to win several rounds in a row.
strategy.intermediate: The 'End-Game' Shuffle: Physical cards often get 'clumped' after a large war. Since wars are often decided by face-cards, if you win a 20-card war, be careful how you order the won cards. Putting your high cards at the very bottom might mean you are vulnerable to a 'War' later when your stack is low.
strategy.advanced: Stamina Management: The game can last a very long time. In competitive settings, 'Card-Tracking' isn't necessary, but mental focus is. If you lose several wars, stay calmâ€”the deck order will cycle back eventually.
tips: If you are playing with 3+ players, the person with the highest card takes everyone's card. If there's a tie, only the tying players go to war.
The Ace is the most powerful card; protect it at all costs by hoping it doesn't get drawn into a war against another Ace.
